title: Big Ten and SEC ban players with professional experience from college competition
dek: On August 25, the Big Ten voted unanimously to prohibit football players who signed pro contracts, appeared on pro rosters, or declared for the NFL Draft as underclassmen from competing in college. The SEC announced a similar policy the same night, extending the ban to basketball players with NBA and WNBA experience. The moves respond to a Louisiana court's temporary restraining order that allowed some players to return to college.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The Big Ten banned players who have signed a professional contract, appeared on a professional roster, or declared for the NFL Draft as an underclassman without withdrawing from maintaining college eligibility; the SEC announced identical football rules plus basketball prohibitions on August 25, 2026.
bottom_line: The bans create a direct legal confrontation: conference rules now prohibit players who already hold state court orders allowing their return. How LSU proceeds with Wright and Harris will reveal whether courts or conferences retain authority. The NCAA, which called such rulings 'destabilizing,' faces its own authority questions as it navigates conflicting judicial and institutional mandates ahead of the August 31 roster cutdown.
body: The Big Ten voted unanimously on Tuesday, August 25, to ban football players who have signed professional contracts, appeared on professional rosters, or declared for the NFL Draft as underclassmen from maintaining eligibility to compete in college. The SEC announced an identical football policy on Tuesday night, and extended the prohibition to men's and women's basketball players with NBA and WNBA experience.

Both conferences acted in direct response to a Louisiana state court's temporary restraining order issued last week. That order allowed a group of players who participated in NFL training camp and preseason to return to college, ruling in their favor on the grounds that they would not have entered the professional process had they known college eligibility would remain available. The court order extends until a hearing on August 31.

The Big Ten's rule prohibits players who declared for the NFL Draft before exhausting all years of eligibility, but contains a narrow exception: players who completed four years and whose names were entered through automatic entry (without underclassman declaration) remain eligible if they were not drafted. Players who participated only in rookie mini-camp tryouts without signing a contract also retain eligibility under the Big Ten policy.

The SEC's rules prohibit teams from including any player who did not appropriately withdraw from the NFL, NBA, or WNBA Drafts, or who signed contracts with those leagues or G-League and WNBA affiliates, or who appeared on any of those rosters at any point. The SEC statement said the conference could assign penalties against member institutions for violations.

The rules have created immediate conflict. At least two former players with Louisiana court injunctions have already signed with LSU. Dae'Quan Wright, a tight end waived by the Browns, secured a deal to play for LSU this fall and will be the first player to transition directly from preseason participation to college. His former Ole Miss teammate, Zxavian Harris, also part of the Louisiana lawsuit, was signed by the Saints but injured before participating in preseason and was waived on August 8; he has also signed with LSU. Under SEC rules, neither would be eligible, yet attorney Darren Heitner, representing Wright, told Front Office Sports on Tuesday night that Wright 'is not only allowed to play, but must be allowed to play,' based on the Louisiana court order, and that LSU intends to honor that directive. The ACC and Big 12 are reportedly having similar policy conversations, and the American is considering a conference-wide ban.

boundary.fixed: Players who completed four years of eligibility and whose names were entered into the draft through the automatic entry process and were not drafted remain eligible under Big Ten rules; players who participated only in rookie mini-camp tryouts but did not sign with a team remain eligible under Big Ten rules
boundary.user_action: The Big Ten rule prohibits conference institutions from maintaining eligibility for athletic competition for affected players; the SEC rule prohibits teams from including affected players and assigns penalties against member institutions for violations
